25.title: The Messenger Hosts of Space
25.b0.ask: “How do the messenger hosts — who judge, counsel, record, and simply stay beside us — help ascending mortals on their long journey?”
25.b2.p: In Paper 24 we looked at the Higher Personalities of the Infinite Spirit. Paper 25 turns to the Messenger Hosts of Space, who rank in the middle of the Infinite Spirit’s family. These versatile beings are the connecting links between the higher personalities and the ministering spirits (25:0.1).
25.b3.p: The messenger hosts are made up of seven groups. Only three of them — the servitals, the conciliators, and the Morontia Companions — are created as such; the other four are levels of attainment reached by the angelic orders. Whatever their place, they always serve under the direction of those who rule the realms to which they are assigned (25:0.2-0.9).
25.b4.p: What, then, does each of these messengers do? And in what form will they stand beside us, from the mansion worlds all the way to the shores of Paradise?
25.b8.t: Created — by the Seven Master Spirits and the Supreme Power Directors
Created — through the Reflective Spirits of the superuniverses
Attained status — drawn from several angelic orders and others
Created — by the local universe Mother Spirits
Attained status — chosen from several angelic orders
25.b9.p: The Havona Servitals are called servitals, but they are not servants in any menial sense. In the spiritual world there is no menial work; all service is sacred and exhilarating (25:1.1). They are the joint creation of the Seven Master Spirits and the Supreme Power Directors and appear in groups of one thousand. Following the law of spirit dominance, they come forth in the ratio of three spiritual beings to one semiphysical (25:1.2-1.4).
25.b10.p: The servitals serve as assistants and associates of the Graduate Guides, helping and instructing the ascenders who have reached Havona. The affection between the two groups runs so deep that there is divine pathos when they part — yet the joy of high duty eclipses the sorrow (25:1.5-1.6). In Orvonton almost 138 billion servitals minister on the 490 educational satellites around the superuniverse capital, inspiring us with the reality and certainty of our eventual graduation (25:1.7).
25.b12.p: For every Havona Servital created, a Universal Conciliator appears in each of the seven superuniverses, through a focalization upon the Reflective Spirits there (25:2.1-2.2). Each superuniverse becomes like a gigantic mirror reflecting the character of the one Master Spirit who presides over it. Because of this, the conciliators together come to hold forty-nine experiential viewpoints (25:2.3-2.4).
25.b13.t: The judicial head, chosen unanimously by the other three
Presents evidence and safeguards the rights of the personalities involved
A quasi-material being who carries out the commission’s decisions
The clerk of the tribunal, who prepares and keeps the records
25.b14.p: The advocate steps aside during adjudication, so a commission in session functions as three; that is why these commissions are sometimes called referee trios (25:2.10). Traveling at the seraphic rate of triple velocity, they are the traveling courts of the worlds, quickly settling minor difficulties. They do not pass on matters of eternal import, so no creature’s soul is ever put in jeopardy by their acts. But once they accept a case, their rulings are final and always unanimous (25:2.11-2.12).
25.b16.p: The conciliators are wholly dependable; not one has ever gone astray. Young commissions begin their work on the lower worlds, worlds like Urantia, and advance step by step to higher levels (25:3.1-3.2).
25.b17.t: Adjust misunderstandings between groups and between different orders of creatures
Adjust minor difficulties among its one hundred systems
Assist the Melchizedeks, the Magisterial Sons, the seraphim, and others
5. Conciliators to the Superuniverse Minor Sectors
The executioner becomes an interpreter of mercy-justice
6. Conciliators to the Superuniverse Major Sectors
They grow from arbiters of differences into explainers of mysteries
Four co-ordinate arbiter-teachers — advisers to the ascending pilgrims
25.b18.p: The moment beings are created with the power of choice, misunderstandings are sure to arise. The Creators could have made the local universes as perfect as Havona. Instead they chose universes that abound in differences and teem with difficulties — and they also provided the means for harmonizing those differences (25:3.7). From level to level the conciliators grow from judges into interpretative teachers, and a group of four serves together forever, just as it was first associated (25:3.12, 3.17).
25.b21.p: The Technical Advisers are the legal and technical minds of the spirit world. At the beginning the Infinite Spirit chose one million of the most orderly minds from among the supernaphim and omniaphim as their nucleus. Ever since, actual experience in applying the laws of perfection to evolutionary creation has been required of all who seek to join them (25:4.1). They are recruited from the supernaphim, seconaphim, tertiaphim, omniaphim, seraphim, and certain types of ascending mortals and midwayers, and in Orvonton they number slightly more than sixty-one trillion (25:4.2-4.10).
25.b22.p: Mortals serve with them only for a time, yet all the way up we act as pupil-teachers, passing on what we have newly learned to those just below us. In the universal regime we are not counted as possessing knowledge and truth until we have shown our ability and our willingness to share it with others (25:4.12).
25.b23.p: The Technical Advisers are the living law libraries of time and space. Such a library cannot be created; it must be evolved by actual experience (25:4.15-4.16). There is always a technique of perfection, a divine method, for doing things, and these advisers know how to guide us in finding that better way (25:4.17).
25.b24.h: 5. The Custodians of Records on Paradise
25.b25.p: Certain senior chief recorders among the tertiary supernaphim of Havona are chosen as keepers of the formal archives of Paradise (25:5.1). Every individual record begins with the recording angels of the inhabited planets and, according to its importance, moves upward through Salvington and the supergovernments. Paradise holds a summary of superuniverse and Havona data, and the cumulative history of the universe of universes is in the custody of these beings (25:5.3).
25.b26.t: More written records, fewer living ones
More living records, fewer formal ones
25.b28.p: The Celestial Recorders are ascendant seraphim from the local universes. Because they can handle spiritual and material energy at the same time, they make every record in duplicate: an original spirit record and a semimaterial counterpart (25:6.1). Thanks to this dual recording, as we ascend we will always be able to consult the history and traditions of our status sphere (25:6.2).
25.b29.p: No falsification has ever been found in their records, and the Mighty Messengers inspect and certify the accuracy of the copies (25:6.3). The senior recorders on Uversa can show the record of everything of cosmic import in Orvonton since the arrival of the Ancients of Days (25:6.6).
25.b31.p: The Morontia Companions are children of the local universe Mother Spirits and the friends and associates of all who live the morontia life. They do not replace the work of the seraphic guardians; they are gracious hosts to those just beginning the long ascent, and they sponsor play (25:7.1). The tasks of the morontia worlds grow steadily harder, but throughout the journey to Paradise there will always be time for rest and spirit play (25:7.2).
25.b32.p: Because they serve only in the local universe, we will truly regret parting from them when we finish the morontia experience. Not until we meet the Paradise Companions will we find another group so devoted to friendship and companionship (25:7.3).
25.b34.p: The Paradise Companions are chosen from among the seraphim, seconaphim, supernaphim, and omniaphim, and this service is the highest honor ever given to the ministering spirits (25:8.1-8.2). They have nothing special to accomplish. They are simply companions, assigned only to be with us and to commune with us as personality associates (25:8.3).
25.b36.p: A companion studies the record of our ascent in advance and warmly welcomes us as we awaken on Paradise from the terminal sleep of time (25:8.5-8.6). Each ascender receives a companion of the same nature as his superuniverse, so a Urantia mortal is met by one of the nature of the Seventh Master Spirit (25:8.8).
25.b37.t: If an ascender fails in Havona
A Paradise Companion goes with him back to the universes of time
A pilgrim who came with his seraphic guardian
The seraphim volunteers to go back with him
A pilgrim whose mortal comrade succeeded
A companion goes with him, while the successful one teaches on Paradise and waits
25.b39.p: The messenger hosts of Paper 25 stand at almost every point along the ascending path. The servitals on the educational worlds assure us that our graduation is certain. The conciliators settle misunderstandings fairly and slowly grow into teachers who interpret. The Technical Advisers show us the better way, the recorders keep our history without a gap, and the Morontia Companions and Paradise Companions stay beside us with no conditions attached. Even if we fail in Havona, we do not go back alone. And at the end of all this care, the verdict that awaits us is not about material success. It asks whether we have been faithful over the essentials.
25.b40.t: There is no menial work; all service is sacred
Commissions of four settle minor disputes quickly and fairly
Conciliators grow from judges into interpretative teachers
Truth is fully possessed only when it is shared
The Custodians of Records on Paradise
The cumulative history of the universe of universes is kept on Paradise
Spirit records with semimaterial copies make the records open to every order
Friends of early ascent who sponsor rest and play
Their whole ministry is simply to be with us
25.b42.box: The messenger hosts judge, teach, record, and stay beside us, so that no ascending mortal is ever left alone anywhere on the way.
26.title: Ministering Spirits of the Central Universe
26.b0.ask: “As the ascending pilgrim crosses the seven circuits of Havona, whose hand does he hold on the way to the Father?”
26.b2.p: In the earlier papers we met the higher personalities and the messengers of the Infinite Spirit’s family. Now Paper 26 comes down to the lowest group of that family, the angelic hosts — but it begins with their highest order, the supernaphim (26:0.1).
26.b3.p: The supernaphim are the ministering spirits of Paradise and the central universe. They are found everywhere from the Isle of Paradise to the worlds of time and space, and no major part of the organized and inhabited creation is without their services (26:0.1). This paper describes in detail the work of the secondary supernaphim, who will one day welcome us to Havona and lead us inward, circuit by circuit.
26.b4.p: So on that final journey across the seven circuits of Havona to the Father, who will help us, and what will we learn?
26.b8.p: Angels are the ministering-spirit associates of the ascending will creatures and the working associates of the divine personalities. Angels of every order are distinct and highly individualized personalities, and they have very social natures, with an associative capacity far beyond that of human beings (26:1.1). The ministering spirits of the grand universe fall into seven orders (26:1.2-1.9).
26.b9.t: The superuniverses — children of the Reflective Spirits
The superuniverses — liaison between the Creator Sons and the Ancients of Days
The superuniverses — exclusive servants of the Seven Supreme Executives
The local universes — offspring of a Universe Mother Spirit
The local universes — assistants of the seraphim
The inhabited worlds — not really of the angelic orders proper
26.b10.p: Their status is not altogether fixed: some cherubim may aspire to seraphic destiny, and evolutionary seraphim can reach the spiritual levels of the ascending Sons of God (26:1.10). The supernaphim, seconaphim, and seraphim together form the unbroken chain of spirit ministers that the Infinite Spirit has provided for all who seek the Father through the Son (26:1.15). They live directly on the spiritual energy of the universe circuits; they “⟦Q 26:1.17⟧have food that you know not⟦/Q⟧” (26:1.17).
26.b11.t: Pair up only when using the Father’s exclusive circuits
The same, and also work in pairs to synchronize with the Son’s circuits
Work singly, but enter the circuits only as liaison pairs
26.b13.p: The supernaphim are skilled ministers to all beings who live on Paradise and in the central universe, and they are created in three major orders (26:2.1). The primary supernaphim help the Paradise Citizens and the ascending pilgrims to understand one another, while the secondary and tertiary orders work on the circuits of Havona (26:2.2-2.4).
26.b14.t: The Seven Master Spirits — seven types
Directing ascenders on the seven circuits of Havona
The Seven Spirits of the Circuits
Specialized ministry on the Havona circuits
26.b15.p: When the Seven Master Spirits create individually, the children of each share their creator’s nature, so the secondary supernaphim come in seven types (26:2.5). The Circuit Spirits seem to have appeared as a creative response of the Master Spirits to the emerging purpose of the Supreme Being (26:2.6). The tertiary supernaphim they create are the older order, so they are considered first (26:2.7).
26.b17.p: The tertiary supernaphim are the angelic specialists of the Havona circuits. Ascending pilgrims pass through Havona from the seventh circuit inward, while the descending pilgrims from Paradise travel from the first circuit outward (26:3.1-3.2). Some may be exempted from one or more of the local universe training worlds, but no pilgrim may avoid passing through all seven circuits of Havona (26:3.2).
26.b18.t: Keep everything moving smoothly, so that nothing can go amiss
Record in triplicate and pass true knowledge to the living libraries of Paradise
Receive and send the broadcasts of the central creation
Carry all messages that need personal delivery
The “living newspapers” of Havona, keeping all informed
Carry beings who are not space traversers
Take up the less exacting duties of their fellows
26.b20.p: The secondary supernaphim serve on the seven circuits of Havona, and half of the order is assigned to training the Paradise pilgrims (26:4.1). In serving the ascending pilgrims they work in seven groups, and each group meets us in turn on its own circuit (26:4.2-4.9). A pilgrim is always tutored by supernaphim who come from the Master Spirit of his own superuniverse, so Urantia mortals will receive special understanding and comfort from supernaphim of the Master Spirit of Orvonton (26:4.10).
26.b22.p: The pilgrim lands on the receiving world of Havona with only one kind of perfection: perfection of purpose. His purpose has been proved, his faith has been tested, and he is known to be disappointment proof (26:4.12-4.13). Faith has won him perfection of purpose, which admits him to the portals of eternity; from now on he must develop perfection of understanding (26:4.14).
26.b23.t: Acceptance of sonship (co-operation with the Adjuster)
26.b25.p: The first we meet are the pilgrim helpers, beings of quick understanding and broad sympathy who welcome the much-traveled ascenders to the settled worlds of the central universe (26:5.1). On the seventh circuit they teach a basic course in three divisions, and here an outline of every Paradise requirement is learned (26:5.2).
26.b26.t: The supreme understanding of the Paradise Trinity
The spiritual comprehension of the Father-Son partnership
The intellectual recognition of the Infinite Spirit
26.b27.p: Long before reaching Havona, the pilgrims have learned to feast upon uncertainty, to fatten upon disappointment, and to invigorate in the presence of difficulties (26:5.3). On the Havona circles time matters little; achievement is the final test. The divinity attainment of this circle is the spiritual recognition of the Master Spirit of one’s own superuniverse (26:5.5).
26.b30.p: Ascenders who move on to the sixth circle are called “spiritual graduates” and come under the supremacy guides, who work only on this circle (26:6.1). Here the ascenders come near to encountering the central universe source of time-space unity — the spiritual reality of God the Supreme (26:6.2).
26.b31.p: The author admits that he is at a loss to explain what happens on this circle. No personal presence of Supremacy can be perceived, yet the ascenders undergo a new integration of consciousness and a new sensitivity to divinity. It seems as if God the Supreme were affectionately bestowing on his experiential children new intellectual grasp and spiritual insight (26:6.3). After satisfying the commission of seventy, they move on to the fifth circuit (26:6.4).
26.b33.p: On the fifth circle the pilgrims are called “⟦Q 26:7.1|26:7.3|26:8.5⟧candidates for the Deity adventure.⟦/Q⟧” They receive advanced teaching about the Trinity in preparation for recognizing the Infinite Spirit as a person, and here they discover what true study and real mental effort mean (26:7.1). Each pilgrim enjoys the undivided attention and whole affection of one Trinity guide (26:7.2).
26.b34.p: The journey to Paradise is a trial trip, and the transit trio goes along (26:7.4). They go not to help the pilgrim locate the Trinity, but to help him in the difficult task of recognizing the Infinite Spirit as a personality (26:7.5).
26.b35.t: A fellow of the finaliters · a director of conduct of the primary supernaphim · a Solitary Messenger or a Trinitized Son
The superaphic circle associate · the Graduate Guide · the Guide’s servital associate
26.b37.p: The fourth circuit is sometimes called the “⟦Q 26:8.1⟧circuit of the Sons.⟦/Q⟧” It is here that the pilgrims of time and the pilgrims of eternity first truly understand one another, and the author says that in many respects this circuit is the most intriguing of the whole Havona sojourn (26:8.1). The Son finders teach their pupils to comprehend the Eternal Son spiritually, to recognize him as a person, and to distinguish him rightly from the Infinite Spirit (26:8.2).
26.b38.p: On the inner circles, advancement is decided purely by the spirituality of the individual, and in the event of failure no one is ever chided (26:8.3). Those who fail on the first adventure return to service in space for not less than a thousand years and then try again; on the second attempt the supernaphim never fail to pilot them through (26:8.5).
26.b40.t: Stage of the first Deity adventure
Almost all from superuniverses three and five
Mostly number six; a few from two and three
26.b42.p: On the third circle the most experienced of the supernaphim, the Father guides, conduct schools of wisdom and colleges of technique. Nothing is neglected that would help a creature of time in the adventure of eternity attainment (26:9.1). Even though circuits still remain to be crossed, the attainment of the Universal Father is the passport to eternity (26:9.2).
26.b43.p: The test of time is almost over, and the command to be perfect has been obeyed. A creature from the very bottom of intelligent existence has risen, proving that the plan of ascension works and showing forever that the Father’s command was just (26:9.3). The broadcasts of Havona flash forth the good news that creatures of animal nature have truly become the perfected sons of God (26:9.4).
26.b45.p: The counselors and advisers of the second circle teach the children of time about the career of eternity (26:10.1). They are also the comforters of those who failed in the Deity adventure. That disappointment differs only in size from the many experiences on which these pilgrims climbed, as on a ladder, from chaos to glory. Certified by the councils of perfection, they return with joy to the service of time (26:10.2-10.4).
26.b46.p: For the successful pilgrims the second circle is pleasant, but it lacks some of the eager anticipation of the earlier circles. Many look back on the long struggle with a joyous envy and wish they could begin it all over again, much as mortals in old age look back on their youth (26:10.5). The counselors prepare them for the last transit sleep, the sleep that always comes between the great stages of the ascending career (26:10.6).
26.b48.p: The innermost circuit is home to a vast and diverse host of beings, and the complements of rest use this setting to prepare the pilgrims for the many groups they will soon meet on Paradise (26:11.1). Here the trinitized sons of mortal finaliters and of Paradise Citizens are gathered and prepared for some future work (26:11.2-11.3).
26.b49.p: The mercy and forbearance that human beings show are not a sign of a manlike God; they are evidence that mortal man is indwelt by the spirit of the living God (26:11.5). The pilgrim goes to sleep on the first circle and awakens on the shores of Paradise, and beside him his long-time associate, the complement of rest, enters that rest with him (26:11.6-11.7).
26.b50.t: Indeed death — on the world of origin
An ideal sleep — the long transit trance before Havona
The true rest — the relaxation of the ages
26.b52.p: Paper 26 does not leave Havona as a mysterious destination. It shows it as a road crossed one circuit at a time. The pilgrim arrives with nothing but perfection of purpose. He learns the basics from the pilgrim helpers, comes to a new realization of God the Supreme, and then seeks in turn the Infinite Spirit, the Son, and the Father. All along the way supernaphim from our own Master Spirit go with us, and even failure is received not with reproach but as a meaningful delay. And when at last we fall into the final sleep, we do not go alone; we awaken on the shores of Paradise as children of eternity.
26.b53.t: Seven orders of angels form an unbroken chain of ministry
Three orders of supernaphim serve Paradise and Havona
The specialists of the seven circuits keep Havona in order
We arrive with perfection of purpose and learn perfection of understanding
In liaison with God, nothing is impossible
On the sixth circle we realize God the Supreme anew
Candidates for the Deity adventure seek the Infinite Spirit as a person
Disappointment is not defeat, and postponement is not disgrace
Attaining the Father is the passport to eternity
Even those who fail are comforted and led to try again
We wake from the final sleep on the shores of Paradise
26.b55.box: On every circuit of Havona the supernaphim stand beside us, and the ability to comprehend carries us to Paradise along the road that the willingness to believe has opened.
27.title: Ministry of the Primary Supernaphim
27.b0.ask: “What must the ascender who has just awakened on Paradise still learn before he can enter eternal service?”
27.b2.p: In Paper 26 we held the hand of the secondary supernaphim as we crossed the seven circuits of Havona. Now Paper 27 brings us to the end of that journey and introduces the primary supernaphim, who greet us on the Isle of Paradise. They have served the Deities from eternity. Never have they departed from the paths of light and righteousness, and not one of their host has ever been lost (27:0.1).
27.b3.p: They work chiefly on Paradise, but they are also placed in command of the seraphim on worlds isolated by rebellion. The present “⟦Q 27:0.2|28:4.11|39:0.9⟧chief of seraphim⟦/Q⟧” on Urantia is the second of this order to serve here since the bestowal of Christ Michael (27:0.2). They minister in seven orders of service, and after arriving on Paradise the ascenders pass through them in reverse order, beginning with the instigators of rest and finishing with the conductors of worship (27:0.3-0.11).
27.b4.p: So when we finally reach Paradise at the end of the long ascent, what is still left for us before the endless career of a finaliter begins?
27.b8.t: Order in which the ascender meets them
Seventh — the end of the training
First — the doorway to the Paradise career
27.b9.p: The instigators of rest are the inspectors of Paradise who go out to the inner circuit of Havona and work there with the complements of rest. The one essential to the enjoyment of Paradise is divine rest, and these are the final instructors who make the pilgrims of time ready for eternity (27:1.1). Rest has a sevenfold nature (27:1.2).
27.b10.t: The rest of sleep and of play
The highest type of spirit personality
Recharging with physical or spiritual energy
Unconscious slumber when enseraphimed, passing from one sphere to another
Transition from one universe status to another
27.b11.p: The last metamorphic sleep carries us across the innermost margins of time and space. We go to sleep in Havona and awaken on Paradise, and we recognize the one who welcomes us as the very instigator of rest who brought on that final sleep. We will remember the last grand stretch of faith, when we once more entrusted our identity to the hands of the Universal Father (27:1.3-1.4). Now there is no more sleep, and God wipes away all tears (27:1.5).
27.b13.p: The chiefs of assignment are the group appointed by the chief supernaphim, “⟦Q 27:2.1⟧the original pattern angel,⟦/Q⟧” to preside over the organization of all three orders of supernaphim. Except for their common head, the first angel of Paradise, the supernaphim are wholly self-governing (27:2.1). On Paradise, study and instruction are not the only occupations; service also plays an essential part in the education that comes before the finaliter corps (27:2.2).
27.b14.p: On Paradise we must get to know more than three thousand orders of Paradise Citizens, the Transcendentalers, and many beings not yet revealed. After long contact with these mighty intellects, it is very restful to visit with angelic types of mind; they remind us of the seraphim with whom we spent so long (27:2.3).
27.b17.p: As we ascend, every new group of associates adds one more level of ethics to be recognized and honored. So by the time we reach Paradise we do not need to be taught ethics, but we do need someone to interpret what we have so laboriously learned as we face so much that is new (27:3.2). The interpreters of ethics help us adjust to many groups of beings from the time we gain residential status until we are inducted into the Corps of Mortal Finaliters (27:3.3).
27.b18.p: All these companionships are mutual. We not only benefit from our associates; we also give each of them something from our own personality and experience. Every one of them is forever different and better for having known an ascending mortal from the evolutionary worlds (27:3.4).
27.b20.p: The proprieties of Paradise are neither meaningless formalities nor artificial castes but inherent courtesies (27:4.1). Harmony is the keynote of the central universe, and proper conduct is essential to progress from knowledge, through philosophy, to spontaneous worship. The spirit of the technique of approaching Divinity is learned in Havona, but its final touches are given only on Paradise (27:4.2).
27.b21.p: All conduct on Paradise is spontaneous and free, yet there is still a proper and perfect way of doing things. The directors of conduct stay beside the “⟦Q 27:4.3⟧strangers within the gates⟦/Q⟧” and guide their steps so that confusion is avoided (27:4.3). For in spite of all the long preparation, Paradise is still inexpressibly strange and new to those who arrive (27:4.4).
27.b23.p: The custodians of knowledge are the “living epistles” of Paradise, the living books of real knowledge. The facts of the universes are actually recorded in them, and it is inherently impossible for an untruth to gain lodgment in their minds (27:5.1). Ask the finders of knowledge at the northern end of the Isle, and the very being who is the thing you wish to know will appear and tell you face to face (27:5.2).
27.b24.p: The wisdom of truth comes from the divinity of the central universe, but experiential knowledge begins largely in time and space (27:5.4). That is why a vast network of recording angels stretches from the local universes to Paradise, and the custodians of knowledge are its final living summary (27:5.3).
27.b25.t: Seven grand orders, each with about one million subdivisions
Not directly accessible; benefited only indirectly, by reflection
Distinct from it — the cumulative summary of universal history
27.b27.p: Next to the supreme satisfaction of worship comes the exhilaration of philosophy. However high we climb, a thousand mysteries remain that call for philosophy (27:6.1). The masters of philosophy are the “⟦Q 27:6.2⟧wise men of heaven⟦/Q⟧”; with them knowledge attains to truth and experience ascends to wisdom (27:6.2).
27.b28.p: At the southern end of Paradise they conduct courses in the seventy functional divisions of wisdom, and although their approaches differ, their final conclusions always agree (27:6.3). One hour’s instruction on Paradise equals ten thousand years of the word-memory methods of Urantia (27:6.4). This philosophy is not broadcast; it is open only to those who are personally present (27:6.6).
27.b29.t: What the ascender on Paradise reaches
They may philosophize — think the truth
They seek to encompass the concepts of the Ultimate and grasp the techniques of the Absolutes
27.b31.p: Worship is the conscious and joyous act of recognizing and acknowledging the intimate, personal relationship of the Creators with their creatures, and its quality is set by the depth of the creature’s perception (27:7.1). The Isle of Paradise is more nearly one vast sanctuary. Through Havona, worship grows circle by circle until on Paradise it becomes a passion that must be directed (27:7.2). No ascender is ever required to enter eternal service until he has found full satisfaction in worship (27:7.3).
27.b32.p: What play does for tired minds on earth, worship does for perfected souls on Paradise — and its spirit can begin to be appreciated even now, here on Urantia (27:7.5). Beings who were perfect from the start can never fully appreciate the overflowing gratitude of those who have climbed up from the depths of darkness, and that worship brings supreme joy to the Deities (27:7.6-7.7).
27.b34.t: The agreement with the Thought Adjuster, when the purpose to survive was sealed
The awakening in the morontia life
The finding of the Universal Father
The Paradise awakening from the final transit slumber
Entrance into the mortal finaliter corps and the beginning of eternal service
27.b35.p: The supernaphim who have attended us ever since our world of origin finally bid us farewell through the conductors of worship as we are mustered into the Corps of the Finality (27:7.9). Now the finaliter stands face to face with the challenge of God the Ultimate (27:7.10).
27.b37.p: Paper 27 shows that arriving on Paradise is not the end but the start of a final education. The instigators of rest wake us on the eternal shores. The chiefs of assignment teach us service; the interpreters of ethics and the directors of conduct teach us to live in harmony with countless beings; the custodians of knowledge and the masters of philosophy teach us to think the truth. And at the top of all this learning stands worship. When the gratitude of creatures who have risen from the depths of darkness satisfies the Father’s infinite love, then at last we enter eternal service as finaliters.
27.b38.t: We wake from the last metamorphic sleep on the eternal shores
Even on Paradise, service is an essential part of education
They help us rightly interpret the ethics we have learned in new relationships
Within spontaneous freedom there is still a perfect way of conduct
We learn face to face from a living library
Knowledge attains to truth and experience ascends to wisdom
Eternal service begins only after full satisfaction in worship
27.b40.box: All the learning of the ascent is completed in worship, and eternal service begins when the creature’s love satisfies the Father’s love.
28.title: Ministering Spirits of the Superuniverses
28.b0.ask: “What do the seconaphim, the living mirrors, show to the rulers of the superuniverses — and what does that mean for us?”
28.b2.p: In Papers 26 and 27 we met the supernaphim, the angels of the central universe and Paradise. Now Paper 28 comes down a level to the superuniverses. As the supernaphim are the angels of the central universe and the seraphim the angels of the local universes, so the seconaphim are the ministering spirits of the superuniverses. Yet in degree of divinity they are much more like supernaphim than seraphim (28:0.1).
28.b3.p: The paper introduces three orders that serve in the superuniverses — the tertiaphim, the omniaphim, and the seconaphim — and gives the most attention to the seconaphim, who are directly involved in mortal ascension (28:0.2-0.6). Reflectivity is part of the very nature of the seconaphim, and they work as living mirrors that can instantly show a being a thousand light-years away.
28.b4.p: What, then, do these living mirrors reflect, and how will our true selves appear when we stand before them?
28.b8.p: The tertiaphim are children of the Infinite Spirit, personalized on Paradise in groups of one thousand; they are the gift of the Infinite Spirit to the Creator Sons of God (28:1.1). When a Michael Son sets out on the universe adventure, a thousand of these companion spirits go with him, and throughout the early times of universe building they are the Creator Son’s only personal staff (28:1.2-1.3).
28.b9.p: When the Bright and Morning Star, the first-born of a local universe, is personalized and the native angels appear, the tertiaphim retire from active service. From then on they are the liaison ministers between the Creator Son and the Ancients of Days of the superuniverse (28:1.3).
28.b11.p: The omniaphim are created by the Infinite Spirit together with the Seven Supreme Executives, and they are the exclusive servants and messengers of these Executives. In Orvonton they keep a colony in the northern parts of Uversa, but they are not registered on Uversa, and they have no direct part in the plan of mortal ascension (28:2.1). They take instructions from, and report to, only the Supreme Executive of Orvonton (28:2.2).
28.b12.t: The Infinite Spirit alone, in groups of one thousand
The Infinite Spirit with the Seven Supreme Executives
The Creator Son, and later liaison service
28.b14.p: The seconaphim are produced in groups of seven by the seven Reflective Spirits at each superuniverse headquarters. Each seven always contains one primary, three secondary, and three tertiary seconaphim (28:3.1). Because they are the offspring of the Reflective Spirits, reflectivity is inherent in their nature, but they do not directly reflect beings that originate solely in the First Source and Center (28:3.2).
28.b15.t: The Divine Counselors · the Perfectors of Wisdom · the Universal Censors
The Mighty Messengers · Those High in Authority · Those without Name and Number
28.b17.p: The primary seconaphim are living mirrors serving the Ancients of Days. By turning to such a mirror, one can see and hear, instantly and without error, the response of a being a thousand or a hundred thousand light-years away. Standing midway between man and God, the Ancients of Days can thus look both ways and know both ways at once (28:4.1). So the supergovernments perfectly reflect the authority above while remaining fully sympathetic to the needs below (28:4.2).
28.b18.t: 1. The Voice of the Conjoint Actor
Interpret the mind of the Infinite Spirit
2. The Voice of the Seven Master Spirits
Portray the collective natures of the Master Spirits
3. The Voice of the Creator Sons
Reflect the minds of the Michaels then and there
4. The Voice of the Angelic Hosts
Give unprejudiced testimony of the sentiments of all angels
Receive a special class of broadcast messages
Carry pilgrims from the superuniverse to Havona
28.b19.p: In all the history of Uversa, the voices of the Creator Sons have never erred (28:4.7). The Ancients of Days deduce the Father’s will by equating the Spirit’s voice from above with the Michaels’ voices from below — and for this all three must act together. This is one reason the superuniverses are always ruled by three Ancients of Days (28:4.10). Even the chief of seraphim on Urantia is aware every day of being drawn upon from Uversa (28:4.11).
28.b21.p: The terms primary, secondary, and tertiary do not mark a difference of status among the seconaphim; they only denote the order of creation (28:5.1). The seven types of secondary seconaphim are divided among three groups of Trinity-origin administrators (28:5.2-5.5).
28.b22.t: The co-ordinated wisdom of the universe of universes
Paradise philosophy, adapted to the lower worlds
The ideals of ethical relationships and teamwork
The counsel of all beings and the facts of space
Reactions of joy and a better taste in humor
The value and satisfactions of unselfish service
True motive and character — “⟦Q 28:5.9|28:5.21⟧what manner of spirit⟦/Q⟧”
28.b23.p: The Unions of Souls help the Perfectors of Wisdom supply the “⟦Q 28:5.13⟧oil of reconciliation⟦/Q⟧” for petty frictions and misunderstandings. One of the most important lessons of mortal life is teamwork, and few are the duties in the universe for the lone servant (28:5.13-5.14). The Joys of Existence try to show that there is inherent joy in freewill existence, independent of outside influences (28:5.16).
28.b24.p: Before the Discerners of Spirits, the Censors stand face to face with the naked soul of the one reflected, which is part of why they can always judge justly (28:5.20). Yet while the presence of the Adjusters can be reflected, the content of the minds of the Mystery Monitors cannot be deciphered (28:5.22).
28.b26.p: The seven types of tertiary seconaphim are assigned collectively to the ascendant Trinitized Sons (28:6.1). What they reflect — origin, mercy, time, trust, service, greatness, and goodness — also serves as a measure of our own character as we ascend.
28.b27.t: Living ready-reference genealogies of all beings
A living trial balance of the mercy extended
The element of time, and the secret of prophecy
The true and the hidden motives of service
28.b28.p: The Memory of Mercy sets our spiritual debts against the saving provision established by the Sons of God. For those who are sincere of purpose and honest of heart, the mercy credit always far exceeds their ability to exhaust it (28:6.5-6.7). But mercy is a quality of growth that can truly appear only after the steps of being just, fair, patient, and kind (28:6.8).
28.b30.p: Trustworthiness is the true measure of self-mastery, of character, and the privilege of service follows as soon as trustworthiness is discovered (28:6.13, 6.16). This magnificent creation was not made just for me; this is not an egocentric universe (28:6.18). On a world like Urantia greatness shows itself in self-control, and the great man is “⟦Q 28:6.20⟧he who subdues his own tongue⟦/Q⟧” (28:6.20). If we can through grace become good, we are thereby becoming great (28:6.22).
28.b32.p: The seconaphim range from the shores of Paradise to the evolutionary worlds of space, and on the four hundred ninety study worlds around Uversa they help with the preparatory course for the university of Havona (28:7.1). The tertiary seconaphim in particular are timesavers, space abridgers, error detectors, faithful teachers, and everlasting guideposts that guide pilgrims at the crossroads of time (28:7.2-7.3).
28.b33.p: But Urantia is still under partial spiritual quarantine, so they cannot function freely here. When the reflective circuits are restored, interplanetary communication will be greatly simplified and quickened; until then the celestial workers joyfully carry on with the means at hand (28:7.4).
28.b35.p: Through the seconaphim, the living mirrors, Paper 28 shows how the rulers of the superuniverses can see and hear far-off places instantly. These mirrors reflect not only the minds of the Gods and the feelings of the angels but also each of us as we are: our origin, our balance of mercy, our use of time, our trustworthiness, and the motives of our service. The deepest truth they reveal is that greatness and goodness cannot be separated. So striving now to become good through grace is the very way we grow in true greatness.
28.b36.t: The Creator Son’s first staff later become liaison ministers
They serve only the Supreme Executives and oversee the superuniverses
Children of the Reflective Spirits, born in groups of seven
Living mirrors instantly show the will of distant beings
They reflect wisdom, counsel, and the true nature of spirits
Greatness and goodness cannot be divorced
Everlasting guideposts for pilgrims at the crossroads
29.title: The Universe Power Directors
29.b0.ask: “Who in the Spirit’s family handles physical energy and keeps the lights and lanes of the universe from failing even for a moment?”
29.b2.p: From Paper 26 through Paper 28 we looked at the ministering angels of the Infinite Spirit’s family. Now Paper 29 introduces the members of that family who have been least understood on Urantia: the controllers and regulators of the physical domain (29:0.1). We have long known that angels exist, but we have heard almost nothing about the living beings who govern energy with intelligence.
29.b3.p: Three groups deal with force and energy in the master universe: the Primary Eventuated Master Force Organizers of Paradise, the Associate Transcendental Master Force Organizers, and the Universe Power Directors (29:0.2-0.4). The power directors are divided in turn into the Seven Supreme Power Directors, the Supreme Power Centers, the Master Physical Controllers, and the Morontia Power Supervisors (29:0.5-0.9). Only on reaching the mansion worlds will we work freely with the Morontia Power Supervisors (29:0.11).
29.b4.p: Who, then, are these unseen keepers of energy, and how do they guard the power of the whole universe without rest?
29.b8.p: The Seven Supreme Power Directors are the physical-energy regulators of the grand universe. Their creation by the Seven Master Spirits is the first recorded case of semimaterial offspring coming from true spirit ancestry (29:1.1). The seven are identical in appearance and function, and no one can tell them apart except by the Master Spirit with whom each is associated (29:1.2).
29.b9.p: Stationed on peripheral Paradise, they regulate the power of the superuniverses singly and that of the central creation collectively (29:1.3). They are the ancestors of the power centers and the physical controllers. The physical-control organization is basically uniform, so to change superuniverse service a controller need only return to Paradise to be retoned (29:1.4).
29.b10.t: Highly spiritual personalities of the angelic order
29.b12.p: Together with the Seven Master Spirits, the Seven Supreme Power Directors produce the Supreme Power Centers (29:2.1). These are beings of high will, endowed with Third-Source personality. They are the intellect of the grand universe power system and the secret of the mind control of the vast network of physical controllers (29:2.9). The fourteen Supreme Power Directors and Supreme Center Supervisors are to universe power what the Master Spirits are to the cosmic mind (29:2.11).
29.b13.t: Seven — regulate the master energy circuits of the grand universe
One million — each supervises a thousand Havona worlds
One thousand on each superuniverse capital
One hundred on each local universe headquarters
Only on special spheres — not one space body in a million
29.b14.p: In Havona there is perfection of energy control, and this is the ultimate goal of all the power centers and physical controllers (29:2.12). The seven power circuits going out from the superuniverse centers are bounded currents of energy, much like the Gulf Stream in the Atlantic. They are stepped down through the local universe, constellation, and system centers until they reach the inhabited worlds (29:2.13-2.18).
29.b16.p: The power centers number more than ten billion, and all are in perfect synchrony with the Seven Supreme Power Directors. They are exempt from all the tribunals of space and are not subject to the direction of either the superuniverse or the local universe governments (29:3.1-3.2). They are created perfect, with no training and no evolution, and they always serve as first assigned (29:3.4). Having no ascendant past to look back on, they never play; they are always on duty (29:3.5).
29.b17.p: They do not create energy, but they modify, manipulate, and direct it. Their only relation to gravity is to resist its pull, so that relation is wholly negative (29:3.6). Each power center is made up of exactly one million units of functional control, works only on specially constructed architectural spheres, and has much to do with the distribution of light without heat (29:3.7, 3.9).
29.b18.t: Seven of the ten forms in each current
The unpredictable realm of the Unqualified Absolute
Nothing whatever to do with them
29.b20.p: The Master Physical Controllers are the mobile subordinates of the Supreme Power Centers and can cross local space at speeds approaching those of the Solitary Messengers (29:4.1). In the superuniverses they are directed by the Council of Equilibrium, which interprets the readings of the master frandalanks (29:4.2). They adjust basic energies not yet discovered on Urantia, making interplanetary transport and communication possible (29:4.14).
29.b22.t: Assign and dispatch all controllers — three billion in Orvonton
The strongest antigravity; ten on Urantia, helping seraphic departures
Living switches and planetary inspectors of seraphic departures
Living superconductors that make distant sights and sounds perceptible
Living catalysts that store energy and release it
The alchemists of space — limitless supplies of energy
Register the presence, pressure, and velocity of force (and time)
29.b23.p: The first three orders are more personal, while the transmitters, associators, dissociators, and frandalanks are wholly automatic in their reactions. Yet all are intelligent; they seem to understand our language but are powerless to answer (29:4.12, 4.26). Even the energy transformers cannot control three of the thirty physical energies, which proves that they are not instruments of the Unqualified Absolute (29:4.25).
29.b24.p: The associators and dissociators are the most slavish of all intelligent creatures, yet they are the first group of life to appear on an organizing material sphere (29:4.34). The dissociators are the alchemists of space, but in all the wonders they work they never transgress the mandates of Cosmic Supremacy (29:4.35). The author suggests that we picture the frandalanks as living machines that work with ultimate precision (29:4.38).
29.b26.p: The Master Force Organizers live on Paradise but work chiefly in unorganized space. They are neither creators nor creatures, and they work only under the supervision of the Architects of the Master Universe (29:5.1-5.4). They function at temperatures that even the power centers of Orvonton could not endure (29:5.7).
29.b27.t: Transmute primordial force into primary energy — nebulae creators
Carry primary energy on to the gravity-energy stage
29.b28.p: When the plans for a local universe are complete and a Creator Son arrives, the associate force organizers give way to the power directors. Where there are no such plans, they remain in charge of the material creations indefinitely, as they now do in outer space (29:5.6).
29.b30.p: Paper 29 shows that behind the light and energy, communication and transport that we take for granted lies the ceaseless labor of living intelligences. From the force organizers who turn primordial force into energy, through the power directors and power centers, down to the physical controllers of a single planet, energy never flows at random. These beings neither play nor rest; they simply do, perfectly, the work they were first given. That even beings with little or no personality serve the universe with intelligence reminds us that the material world, too, rests in the care of the Infinite Spirit.
29.b31.t: The first semimaterial offspring of spirit ancestry regulate energy
Seven levels of centers step power down to the inhabited worlds
Created perfect, they never for a moment leave their post
Even impersonal intelligence is put to work in the service of energy
They organize primordial force into the material for new universes
29.b33.box: Through the ceaseless labor of the unseen power directors, the material universe too rests in the intelligent care of the Infinite Spirit.
30.title: Personalities of the Grand Universe
30.b0.ask: “Among the countless beings of the universe, what place does the ascending mortal hold, and what path does he walk?”
30.b2.p: Up to Paper 29 we met one group of beings after another, from the family of the Infinite Spirit to the Universe Power Directors. Now Paper 30 gathers them all in one place and sorts them out. The personalities and other-than-personal entities functioning on Paradise and in the grand universe are so many that even the number of major orders would stagger the human imagination (30:0.1).
30.b3.p: So this paper offers two classifications: a suggestion of the Paradise classification and an abbreviation of the Uversa Personality Register (30:0.1). Not every group is revealed, however. Too much revelation would stifle imagination, so room is deliberately left for the creative speculation of thinking mortals over the next thousand years (30:0.2).
30.b4.p: Where, then, do we mortals stand in this endless list of beings, and through what stages will we reach Paradise?
30.b7.h: 1. The Paradise Classification of Living Beings
30.b8.p: On Paradise, living beings are classified by their inherent and attained relationship to the Paradise Deities. That is why, at the great gatherings, those present are often grouped by origin: triune origin, dual origin, and single origin (30:1.1). To these are added the eventuated Transcendentalers, the fragments of Deity, the superpersonal beings, and orders not yet revealed (30:1.92-1.104).
30.b9.t: All three Deities or the Trinity — the Supreme Spirits, the Stationary Sons of the Trinity, the Paradise Citizens
Two Deities, or two of their offspring — Creator Sons, Melchizedeks, Adjuster-fused mortals
One Deity, or one of its offspring — Universe Mother Spirits, the angels, the power directors
Neither creators nor creatures — the Architects of the Master Universe
The Thought Adjusters and other fragments
Majeston, the Midsonite orders, and others
30.b10.p: By origin, we mortals end up in a surprising place. Adjuster-fused mortals belong to the ascending orders of dual-origin beings, because they become one with the Adjuster, a fragment of the Father (30:1.50, 1.100). Those who fuse with a fragment of the spirit of the Third Source and Center become Spirit-fused mortals, and those united with the individualized spirit of a Creator Son become Son-fused mortals (30:1.101-1.102).
30.b12.p: There are no personalities of “pure mind.” No entity has personality unless God, who is spirit, gives it, and a mind not associated with either spiritual or physical energy is not a personality (30:1.113). The author says that because we are persons, beings who are personalized can be described to us — but how could an absonitized being ever be explained (30:1.114)?
30.b14.p: On Uversa the divine family of living beings is registered in seven grand divisions (30:2.1-2.8). The list chiefly shows the beings we will meet on our way up to Paradise; it leaves out the vast orders that do their work apart from the plan of mortal ascension (30:2.9).
30.b15.t: Grand division of the Uversa register
The Universal Father · the Eternal Son · the Infinite Spirit
The Seven Master Spirits, the Supreme Executives, the Reflective Spirits, the adjutant mind-spirits
The Days orders, the Perfectors of Wisdom, the Havona Natives
Descending Sons · Ascending Sons · Trinitized Sons
V. Personalities of the Infinite Spirit
Higher Personalities · the Messenger Hosts of Space · the ministering spirits
Supreme Power Directors, power centers, physical and morontia controllers
VII. The Corps of Permanent Citizenship
Midwayers, Adamic Sons, Susatia, Paradise Citizens, and others
30.b16.p: Ascending mortals are registered in the fourth division, the Sons of God, as “Ascending Sons.” Father-fused, Son-fused, and Spirit-fused mortals are listed there side by side with evolutionary seraphim, ascending Material Sons, translated midwayers, and Personalized Adjusters (30:2.46-2.53).
30.b17.t: The Paradise Corps of the Finality
Seven corps, including the Corps of Mortal Finaliters
Bright and Morning Stars, Brilliant Evening Stars, Archangels, Mansion World Teachers, and others
From the Star Students to the Ascending Pilgrims
30.b19.p: The seven courtesy colonies are guests who stay for a time on architectural spheres such as Uversa while carrying out special assignments (30:3.1). Uversa alone has more than a million star observers and more than a billion student visitors (30:3.4, 3.11). Except on Paradise, knowledge is not inherent, so our understanding of the physical universe depends largely on observation and research (30:3.5).
30.b20.t: Celestial astronomers — anyone may join, but must serve a millennium
Promote relaxation and humor — reversion to past memories
Run preparatory schools for the next world
Observers and exchange pupils — half are stopovers
Largely self-governing colonies while assigned to service
30.b21.p: The whole plan of mortal ascension is marked by giving out new truth and experience to others as soon as we gain them (30:3.9). And the human desire to travel and to see new peoples and worlds will be fully satisfied on the long climb to Paradise (30:3.12).
30.b23.p: Mortals are all evolutionary beings of animal origin with the potential to ascend, and in origin, nature, and destiny they are not wholly unlike the peoples of Urantia (30:4.10). The author lays out, in seven stages, the career of an Adjuster-fused mortal — a destiny that all the human races of Urantia may anticipate (30:4.1-4.9).
30.b24.t: Without a personal guardian, they sleep until the end of the dispensation
Resurrected in morontia form on the seven mansion worlds
Pass through system, constellation, and universe to real spirit identity
Trained as young spirits under the Ancients of Days
Travel alone and receive individual spiritual education
Find God and are mustered into the Corps of the Finality
30.b25.p: The passing of time means nothing to a sleeping survivor: one who has slept five thousand years will wake no differently from one who rested five days (30:4.12). Resurrection is the reuniting of the spirit transcript of the mind, kept by the Adjuster, with the immortal soul, kept by the seraphim (30:4.15). When Jesus said, “⟦Q 30:4.17⟧In my Father’s house are many mansions,⟦/Q⟧” he was speaking of these training worlds (30:4.17).
30.b26.p: Once mortals receive spirit confirmation before leaving the local universe, their status is settled forever; superuniverse wards have never been known to go astray (30:4.21). On arriving in Havona, the first act is to thank the transport seconaphim, and then to send a message of thanksgiving and adoration to the Creator Son (30:4.28). Of all the creatures of the grand universe, only those who are Father fused are mustered into the Mortal Corps of the Finality (30:4.31).
30.b28.p: Paper 30 spreads the beings of the universe out in a seemingly endless list, but its purpose is not to overwhelm us. It is to show us the place we mortals hold among countless beings. A lowly creature of animal origin fuses with the Adjuster, is registered as an ascending son of God, and passes in turn through sleep, resurrection, and training until it reaches Paradise. And at every stage of that long school, we climb by passing on what we have learned to those who come after us.
30.b29.t: The Paradise Classification of Living Beings
All beings are classified by their origin and their relation to the Deities
Ascending mortals are registered among the Sons of God
Sharing what we learn at once is the mark of the ascension plan
Through seven stages the mortal becomes a finaliter
30.b31.box: Even among endless orders of beings, the mortal is recorded as an ascending son of God, and he climbs to Paradise by learning and by sharing what he learns.
31.title: The Corps of the Finality
31.b0.ask: “For the mortal who has found God and reached Paradise, what destiny waits beyond?”
31.b2.p: In Paper 30 we followed the seven stages of the ascent, from planetary mortal to Paradise arrival. Now Paper 31 takes up the present known destination of that road, the Corps of Mortal Finaliters, and with it brings this series of thirty-one papers to a close (31:0.1). Glorified mortals are not alone in this corps; several other groups are assigned to it as well (31:0.2-0.7).
31.b3.p: The Corps of the Finality is a wholly self-governing body. It chooses its own leaders, and its oath of allegiance is only to the Paradise Trinity (31:0.12). All its members are received in equality, yet that equality in no way erases individuality (31:0.9). They are the tried and true souls of time and space — the evolutionary salt of the universe — and one or more companies of them are always serving on Urantia (31:0.11, 0.13).
31.b4.p: Who, then, make up the finaliters, and why do the Gods train them so thoroughly?
31.b8.t: Members of the primary finaliter corps
Places in a company of one thousand
Included above — far fewer than the mortals
31.b9.p: Many of the Havona natives who teach the pilgrims become greatly attached to the ascending mortals and long to join the Corps of the Finality; millions upon millions of them are on the waiting list (31:1.1). They bring the viewpoint of one born in perfection, so the finaliters embrace both kinds of experience — the perfect and the perfected (31:1.1).
31.b10.p: Havona natives are received in the ratio of one in a thousand. A company is made up of one Havona native, one Gravity Messenger, and 997 ascendant creatures, and the oath is taken individually (31:1.3). The possibility of becoming a finaliter is one of the supreme adventures of these perfect races (31:1.4).
31.b12.p: The Gravity Messengers come from Divinington; they are modified and personalized Adjusters. They are under the exclusive jurisdiction of Grandfanda and are assigned only to the primary Corps of the Finality. They can transcend time and space and seem able to use any and all energies, circuits, and even gravity (31:2.1-2.2). Mortal finaliters cannot defy time and space, but these superspirit beings, who can, serve under their command (31:2.2).
31.b13.p: Gravity Messengers and mortal finaliters come to share a deep affection. One is a direct personalization of a fragment of the Father; the other is an immortal soul fused with a fragment of that same Father (31:2.4).
31.b15.p: Adjuster-fused mortals make up the bulk of the primary Corps of the Finality (31:3.1). At present they serve for a time in the Corps of Light and Life, but such a long course of training must be meant to prepare them for still greater trust and responsibility (31:3.2). And it is worth noting that they are recorded as only sixth-stage spirits (31:3.3).
31.b16.t: During the sojourn in the minor sectors
On translation to the major sectors
On going to the central training worlds of the superuniverse
On reaching the sixth circle of Havona
Unrevealed assignment and attainment of God the Supreme
31.b17.t: What they have not yet attained
The present limit of spirit progression
The present limit of creature perfection
31.b18.p: The authors say that human beings are entitled to share their opinions and to conjecture with them about this mystery. And they ask: Why should the Gods be so concerned to train surviving mortals so thoroughly in the technique of universe management (31:3.8)?
31.b20.p: Many faithful seraphic guardians are allowed to go through the ascending career with their human wards. After becoming Father fused, they take the finaliter oath alongside their wards and forever accept the destiny of their mortal associates (31:4.1). The angel who guarded us on earth may become our companion for eternity.
31.b22.p: Adamic citizens long delayed in receiving a planetary assignment, or a planetary Adam and Eve on a world in the later eras of light and life, may receive Adjusters and set out on the ascent (31:5.1-5.2). Material Sons who partially fail in their mission, as Adam did on Urantia, take the natural course of the peoples of the realm — death, and then the ascent by faith — and so reach the Corps of the Finality (31:5.2).
31.b23.p: Not many companies include Material Sons, but where they are present they are invariably chosen as leaders. When both of an Edenic pair are in the same group, they function together as one personality, and they are far more successful in trinitizing than ascending mortals (31:5.3).
31.b25.p: When their native world is settled in light and life, the midway creatures are released from permanent citizenship and ascend with the mortals through the morontia worlds, the superuniverse, and Havona (31:6.1). The secondary midwayers are all eventually Adjuster fused and mustered into the mortal corps (31:6.2).
31.b27.p: At present every finaliter company has only 999 permanent members of oath status. The vacant place is filled by the chief of the Evangels of Light attached for a given mission (31:7.1). The Evangels of Light do not take the finaliter oath, and when their attachment ends they return to their former status (31:7.2).
31.b28.p: There are now just six classes of permanent members, so there is much speculation about who the seventh group will be. Some think of the trinitized beings; one author thinks it will be beings native to the new universe of future service; the other inclines toward some Paradise personality not yet created. We will probably not really know until the finaliters enter the seventh stage of spirit (31:7.3-7.5).
31.b30.p: Part of the finaliter’s experience on Paradise is the effort to understand the more than one thousand groups of Transcendentalers who live in the west of Paradise (31:8.1). They are neither creators nor creatures; they simply eventuate. They have nothing to do with Havona or the superuniverses but are concerned only with the superadministration of the master universe, and they are subject to God the Ultimate (31:8.2-8.3).
31.b31.p: A mortal’s first serious contact with a Transcendentaler comes when he stands in the finaliter receiving circle and the chief of Transcendentalers administers the Trinity oath of eternity (31:8.4).
31.b33.p: The Architects of the Master Universe are the governing corps of the Transcendentalers. They number 28,011, and their origin, nature, and destiny may not be fully revealed (31:9.1-9.2). They exist on seven levels of the absonite and are thought to be concerned even with the plans for the four universes of outer space (31:9.3-9.9).
31.b34.t: 1 — the senior Architect: Paradise and its twenty-one worlds
3 — the billion spheres of the central universe
7 — the superco-ordinators of the grand universe
70 — the first universe of outer space
490 — the second universe of outer space
3,430 — the third universe of outer space
24,010 — the fourth universe of outer space
31.b35.p: A Paradise tradition holds that the eventuation of a 28,012th Architect was attempted but that this being experienced personality seizure by the Universal Absolute; the series seems to have reached the limit of absonity with the 28,011th (31:9.10). The Architects give technical approval to the space sites of the Creator Sons, and together with them and the Supreme Being they form the Trinity Ultimate (31:9.14).
31.b37.p: The senior Master Architect oversees the seven Corps of the Finality, and the heads of the seven corps form the Supreme Council of Destiny; in this universe age Grandfanda, the first mortal ascender, is its chief (31:10.1-10.9). Nothing like this mobilization has happened since the rulers of the seven superuniverses were commissioned; it is the divinity response to the future needs of the outer universes (31:10.10).
31.b38.t: The seven Corps of the Finality
The Corps of Conjoint Trinitized Finaliters
The Corps of Unrevealed Sons of Destiny
31.b39.p: The outer universes will come into being without any share in the evolution of the Supreme Being. We now face difficulties because the sovereignty of God the Supreme is still incomplete, but we are sharing the unique experience of his evolution (31:10.11-10.12). So the mission of the finaliters may be to carry this experience out to the outer universes, administering them and making up for what they lack (31:10.13).
31.b41.t: Three developments of which we are certain
Vast new universes are organizing in outer space
Perfected ascenders are being mobilized on Paradise
The Supreme Being is powerizing as sovereign of the supercreations
31.b43.p: Paper 31 shows that reaching Paradise is not the end of the ascent but the threshold of a greater adventure. Mortals, seraphim, Havona natives, Material Sons, midwayers, and Gravity Messengers take the oath together and form the Corps of the Finality. Yet they are still only sixth-stage spirits, and the seventh place and the seventh stage remain open. New universes are gathering in outer space, the Supreme Being is powerizing, and the finaliters wait on Paradise for their next assignment. Our own experience of living through the evolution of the Supreme will one day be the capital with which we serve those universes. No destiny could be more glorious for children of animal origin.
31.b44.t: The perfect and the perfected form one corps
Messengers who transcend time and space serve under the finaliters
Guardian angels share their mortal companions’ destiny forever
Even a defaulting Adam reaches the finality by the ascent of faith
Midwayers too at last attain Paradise finality
One place in each company, and the seventh class, are still open
Beings who are neither creators nor creatures administer the oath
28,011 Architects plan even the outer universes
The finaliters await a destiny of service to the outer universes
31.b46.box: The experience of mortals who have evolved together with the Supreme Being leads on to the glorious destiny of serving, as finaliters, universes yet to come.
32.title: The Evolution of Local Universes
32.b0.ask: “Why does a Creator Son build a universe that grows, rather than one that is finished from the start?”
32.b2.p: In the earlier papers we met the many orders of sons and spirits who rule and serve the local universe. Now Paper 32 shows the stage on which they work — how the local universe itself comes into being and grows. A local universe is the handiwork of a Creator Son of the order of Michael. It is made up of one hundred constellations and ten thousand systems, and in the end some one million inhabited worlds (32:0.1).
32.b3.p: These universes of time and space are all evolutionary. The creative plan of the Michaels always follows the path of gradual development of the physical, intellectual, and spiritual natures and capacities of their creatures (32:0.2). The sovereign of our universe, Nebadon, is Jesus of Nazareth and Michael of Salvington, and all his plans were fully approved by the Paradise Trinity (32:0.3).
32.b4.p: Why, then, did God not make a perfect universe from the beginning? Why choose a slow road that starts from scattered energy and lets mortals climb one rung at a time?
32.b8.p: A local universe is prepared before its Creator Son arrives. The Master Force Organizers of Paradise work with the primordial energies, and when energy begins to respond to gravity, they give way to the power directors of the superuniverse (32:1.1). Only after the power directors have gathered enough energy to provide the material for suns and spheres can a Creator Son begin to organize (32:1.2).
32.b9.t: The Master Force Organizers of Paradise
The superuniverse power directors, working alone
The Creator Son arrives with a Creative Daughter of the Infinite Spirit
Universe headquarters, then constellation headquarters, then system capitals
32.b10.p: Local universes have about the same energy potential, but they differ in size and in the amount of visible matter (32:1.3). The energy charge of a local universe is roughly one one-hundred-thousandth of that of its superuniverse, and the only physical limit on the growth of Nebadon is the amount of space-energy held by gravity control (32:1.4). As soon as the Creator Son arrives, work begins on the architectural sphere that will become the headquarters world (32:1.5).
32.b12.p: Michael built the inhabited realms of Nebadon from energies the power directors had already organized, and the same hundred power centers who first worked with him still serve on Salvington (32:2.1-2.2). The first act of creation was the organization of the headquarters world, Salvington, and a little over a billion years passed before its living staff arrived. Then came the hundred constellation headquarters and the ten thousand system headquarters (32:2.3).
32.b13.p: When the physical plan is finished, the Creator Son and the Creative Spirit begin the creation of life. The first result is the Bright and Morning Star, the chief executive of the universe. Then come the sons and daughters of the local universe and its government, and finally the Creator Son enters into the Father’s proposal to create mortal man in the divine image (32:2.6-2.8).
32.b14.t: Salvington and its architectural satellites; constellation and system headquarters
The Creator Son’s first creative concept and chief executive
3. Sons and daughters, and the government
From the supreme councils down to the Planetary Princes
In the divine image, according to the Father’s proposal
32.b15.p: Nebadon is still a young cluster in Orvonton, so the organization of planets goes on; at the last registry there were 3,840,101 inhabited planets (32:2.9). The 619 inhabited worlds of our system, Satania, are scattered among more than five hundred physical systems. Satania lies on the edge of the local universe, and Nebadon lies well out toward the edge of Orvonton (32:2.10-2.11).
32.b16.t: 619, scattered among over five hundred physical systems
From Jerusem to the center of the superuniverse
Seven, including Avalon, Henselon, Sanselon, and Portalon
32.b18.p: The only creation that is perfectly settled is Havona, the central universe; the seven superuniverses are finite, evolutionary, and steadily progressive (32:3.1). Outside the central universe, perfection is a progressive attainment, and the plans of the Creator Sons for evolving their universes show an almost infinite variety (32:3.3).
32.b19.p: Here there is a wise compensation. In the central universe the Father is personally present but absent from the minds of his children. In the universes of space he is absent in person but intimately present in the minds of his mortal children through the Adjusters (32:3.4). The farther down we go, the harder it is to find the unseen Father, so the surest safeguard is to hold on firmly to the truth that the Father is present in his Sons (32:3.6).
32.b20.t: Personally present, but absent from the minds of his children
Absent in person, but present in mortal minds through the Adjusters
32.b22.p: The perfection that creatures of time reach is wholly an acquirement, a genuine personal possession (32:3.9). Animal origin is no stigma; those who begin at the bottom and climb the ladder round by round gain an experience that knows every phase of life. It would have been just as easy for the Father to make everyone perfect, but that would have taken away the wonderful experience of adventure and training (32:3.10-3.11). Innate perfection and evolved perfection differ only in kind, and each needs the other (32:3.14-3.15).
32.b23.t: What each needs from the other
The superuniverses, for the development of those who descend
Havona, for the final training of those who ascend
32.b24.h: 4. God’s Relation to a Local Universe
32.b25.p: Because the Father has delegated so much, we should not think of him as silent or inactive. He is the silent member only in the sense that he never does anything that another can do (32:4.1). God knows that his creatures need function and experience, so he withdraws from activity — yet even in that withdrawal he takes an actual, personal part through the agencies and personalities he has ordained (32:4.2).
32.b26.p: In the administration of a local universe, the law of the Creator Son and the policies of those under him always prevail; there is no division of authority (32:4.3). At the same time the Father is actually present in mortals through the indwelling Adjuster and is the source of their personality (32:4.5). The Adjusters are not directly co-ordinated with the government of the local universe, and through the personality circuit the Father personally knows all the thoughts and acts of every being (32:4.6, 4.8).
32.b27.t: In the person of the Creator Son
The policies and administration of the local universe
A fragment of his prepersonal spirit in the depths of the mortal mind
Personal knowledge of all the thoughts and acts of all beings
By one of the Seven Master Spirits
Spiritually present in the universe and in our hearts
32.b28.p: God is not a self-centered personality. He has given up every function that another being can perform, and from what he has kept back he gives the Thought Adjusters to mortals (32:4.10-4.11). The Father has poured himself out to make all creation rich (32:4.12).
32.b30.p: There is a great and glorious purpose in the march of the universes, and none of our mortal struggle is in vain. We are all part of an eternal project that the Gods are supervising (32:5.1). The events of time and the struggles of material life are only the transient scaffolding that bridges over to the promised land of spiritual reality (32:5.2).
32.b31.p: The author suggests that we think of eternity not as a straight line but as an endless circle, a cycle. The sectors of time are born, live, and die, but those who survive go on as part of eternity, swinging forever around the circle of the eternal ages (32:5.4-5.5). He frankly admits that eternity cannot be fully grasped by a finite mind, yet he tries to help our thoughts take shape (32:5.6).
32.b32.t: A straightaway line of events with a beginning and an end
An endless circle, synchronized with the cycles of time
32.b34.p: God’s plan is one of boundless opportunity, unlimited progress, and endless life, and its treasures are ours for the striving (32:5.7). Whoever will may enter, and certain victory will crown everyone who runs the race of faith and trust, depending on the indwelling Adjuster and the spirit of the Universe Son (32:5.8).
32.b36.p: Paper 32 shows the local universe growing in stages: from the gathering of energy by the power directors, to Salvington and the architectural worlds, to the Bright and Morning Star and the sons and daughters, and at last to mortal man. This slow evolution is not a flaw but wisdom. Instead of receiving perfection as a gift, we are meant to earn it one rung at a time, and the perfection gained this way joins with innate perfection to make the universe whole. Throughout it all the Father may seem to stand far back, yet he is present in the Creator Son, in the personality circuit, and in the Adjuster deep within our minds. So our struggles are not in vain, and the race for perfection is open to anyone who will.
32.b37.t: The Creator Son comes only after the power directors have gathered energy
Creation proceeds from the physical foundation, to the Morning Star, to government, to mortal man
Perfection is a true possession, earned one rung at a time
God’s Relation to a Local Universe
The Father seems withdrawn, yet takes part through every channel
Mortal struggle is not in vain, and the race for perfection is open
32.b39.box: God gave us a growing universe instead of a finished one, and he has given us himself that we may be like him.
